title: My sets/frequency for Natural Hypertrophy
summary: NH describes his upper/lower split, 6 days a week with Sunday off, where upper days rotate between bench days and arm days so he never benches three times a week. He squats high bar only every 8 days but has knee flexion on most lower days, pulls from the floor every 4 days, trains arms every upper day, and aims to stimulate muscles every 48 hours. Sets: 1-3 heavy sets, 4 sets for accessories, overhead press and pin press with back-off sets in between, and 6-7 sets for low-impact rehab-like movements.

claims.claim: NH builds each workout around a main lift and runs an upper/lower split: lower days train only lower body, upper days only upper body.
He trains 6 days a week and takes Sunday off.
Benching competition-style three times a week is a recipe for disaster; NH tried it while powerlifting and it leads to nagging shoulder pain.

His three upper days rotate between bench days and arm days (two bench + one arm or two arm + one bench in a week), and bench days are always separated by an arm day, e.g. bench Monday, arms Wednesday, bench Friday.

He back squats (high bar) only every 8 days, so some weeks have no squats, but three of his four lower days include a knee-flexion movement such as front squat or safety-bar squat, which deload the knee.
NH damaged his right knee playing football and his left knee playing basketball, so his legs take a long time to warm up.
Because warm-up takes so long, on squat day he does a lot of volume: at least 11-12 heavy squats while his knees are warm.
He pulls deadlifts from the floor every 4 days and has one other day with Romanian deadlifts from the rack to go through the hinge range of motion.
Arms are what he trains most often: every upper-body day includes an elbow-flexion biceps movement.
He alternates days where a muscle is annihilated with days where it is only lightly stimulated, but never leaves a muscle untrained.
A lower-body day without both knee flexion and a hinge is incomplete; every upper day, even arm day, includes some movement to send blood to the chest for recovery and health.
For naturals, protein synthesis runs on roughly a 48-hour cycle after training, so stimulating each muscle about every 48 hours drives growth.
Heavy movements get only 1-3 sets, never 5 or 10; one heavy set means more accessory volume afterwards, three means easier accessories.
Accessories are almost always 4 sets: 2 is not enough and 5 is too much for him.
Overhead press gets 3 top sets with a back-off set after each (e.g. 155 lb x5 then strip to 135 lb x5), making 6 sets; pin press likewise goes from 4 to 8 sets.
Low-impact, rehab-like movements (back hyperextensions, pull-ups, push-ups) get 6-7 sets, usually 6.

exercises.name: High-bar back squat
cues: 11-12+ heavy reps once knees are warm
exercises.why: knees need long warm-up, so volume is concentrated

exercises.name: Front squat / safety-bar squat
exercises.why: knee flexion that deloads the knee on other lower days

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift from the rack
exercises.why: hinge range of motion without a floor pull
